title: LẤY GỐC TIẾNG ANH V-ACT - ĐỀ SỐ 10
notes: Chưa có đáp án trong dữ liệu nguồn; hệ thống không chấm điểm đề này.

questions.content: By the time the audit was completed, several inconsistencies _______ in the financial statements.
options: A. have emerged
B. had emerged
C. were emerging
D. are emerging

questions.content: Given the current data trends, the new policy is _______ to face resistance than policymakers initially expected.
options: A. more likely
B. as likely
C. less likely
D. the most likely

questions.content: _______ information has been released so far, making it difficult to assess the full impact of the decision.
options: A. Little
B. Many
C. Few
D. A few

questions.content: The report highlights the need for a more _______ approach to regulating emerging technologies.
options: A. systematically
B. Systematize
C. systematic
D. systemization

questions.content: Despite repeated warnings, the committee decided to _______ the proposal until more evidence became available.
options: A. press on with
B. put off
C. carry out
D. hold up

questions.content: The analyst <u>whom </u>the report refers to<u> claims that </u>renewable energy projects <u>require more funding</u> than <u>they initially expected</u>.
options: A. whom
B. the report refers to
C. require more funding
D. they initially expected

questions.content: After months of negotiation, the board finally<u> went through</u> with the plan, despite several members<u> having voiced</u>serious concerns about<u>its long-term</u> <u>financial viability</u>
options: A. went through
B. having voiced
C. its long-term
D. financial viability

questions.content: The company acknowledged<u> the employees’ </u>concerns but emphasized that <u>last year </u>profit was largely affected <u>by external</u> <u>market shocks.</u>
options: A. the employees’
B. last year
C. by external
D. market shocks

questions.content: A range of policy options <u>remain </u>under discussion, but only one of them <u>appear</u> to satisfy <u>both economic</u> and <u>environmental priorities</u>.
options: A. remain
B. Appear
C. both economic
D. environmental priorities

questions.content: She has been appointed <u>the</u> head of <u>an</u> independent research institute <u>focusing on</u> <u>climate resilience</u>.
options: A. climate resilience
B. an
C. focusing on
D. the

questions.content: “I didn’t reject the proposal because it lacked merit,” she explained.
options: A. She explained that she hadn’t rejected the proposal since it lacked merit.
B. She explained that she didn’t reject the proposal due to its lack of merit.
C. She explained that she hadn’t rejected the proposal because it lacked merit.
D. She explained that she wouldn’t reject the proposal for lacking merit.

questions.content: If she were more cautious, she wouldn’t have approved the proposal so quickly.
options: A. She is cautious, so she approved it quickly.
B. She wasn’t cautious, but she didn’t approve it quickly.
C. Because she was cautious, she approved it quickly.
D. Her lack of caution led to quick approval.

questions.content: People expect the results to be released earlier than anticipated.
options: A. The results are expected to be released early.
B. The results were expected to release earlier.
C. It is expected people will release results early.
D. The results expect early release.

questions.content: “Under no circumstances should employees disclose internal data.”
options: A. Employees were warned about internal data.
B. Employees were forbidden to disclose internal data.
C. Employees were advised not to disclose data.
D. Employees were reminded about data disclosure.

questions.content: Not many solutions proposed so far are as cost-effective as this one.
options: A. This solution is the only cost-effective one.
B. Every solution proposed so far is less cost-effective than this one.
C. This solution is among the most cost-effective.
D. No solution is as cost-effective as this one.

questions.content: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A. how extensive medical interventions drastically increase lifespan
B. how realistic small changes in daily habits can promote longevity
C. how diet alone is more important than sleep or exercise for health
D. how remaining sedentary affects overall disease risk

questions.content: In the passage, what does “they” refer to in “they add up to meaningful improvements”?
options: A. several additional years of life and healthspan
B. people with the poorest health behaviours
C. small changes in sleep, exercise and diet
D. major diseases such as heart disease and cancer

questions.content: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage as part of the healthy lifestyle improvements?
options: A. getting more sleep at night
B. increasing diet quality with more whole grains
C. reducing sedentary time by taking regular breaks
D. adding a few extra minutes of exercise each day

questions.content: What is a detailed finding from the research described in the passage?
options: A. Combining extra sleep, exercise and better diet was linked to additional years of life.
B. People who completely overhauled their habits lived longer than anyone else.
C. Only diet changes mattered for health gains, not sleep or exercise.
D. Sleep alone, increasing by five minutes, guaranteed longer life.

questions.content: Which of the following best restates the meaning of “modest improvements” as used in the passage?
options: A. major upgrades in people’s lifestyles
B. small but manageable changes in daily habits
C. changes that are primarily expensive and difficult
D. temporary adjustments that have no long-term impact

questions.content: What can be inferred about the type of changes the researchers wanted people to make?
options: A. They preferred changes that require extensive training and supervision.
B. They thought exercise was more important than sleep or diet.
C. They believed only diet changes matter regardless of other habits.
D. They were focused on changes people can realistically sustain.

questions.content: Which of the following words is CLOSEST in meaning to vigorous in paragraph 1?
options: A. intense
B. persistent
C. strenuous
D. animated

questions.content: Which of the following would be the most suitable title for the passage?
options: A. The Evolution of Big Air Skiing at the Olympics
B. Colby Stevenson’s Unexpected Path to Olympic Silver
C. Why Slopestyle Skiers Dominate the Winter Games
D. Norway’s Continued Success in Freestyle Skiing

questions.content: According to Paragraph 1, which factor most directly contributed to Stevenson securing the silver medal?
options: A. His prior dominance in slopestyle events
B. The difficulty of the trick he successfully landed
C. The judges’ preference for American athletes
D. The mistakes made by his closest competitors

questions.content: According to the passage, which detail is TRUE?
options: A. Stevenson had extensive big air experience before the Olympics.
B. Stevenson won gold in both big air and slopestyle.
C. Stevenson suffered serious injuries in a car accident.
D. Stevenson retired from skiing after the accident.

questions.content: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage?
options: A. The country Stevenson represents
B. The type of injury Stevenson suffered
C. The support Stevenson received from others
D. The judges’ scoring criteria in big air

questions.content: Which of the following would the author most likely agree with?
options: A. Persistence can help athletes overcome major obstacles.
B. Olympic medals are largely a matter of luck.
C. Athletic success depends mainly on natural talent.
D. Specialization in one discipline guarantees Olympic success.

questions.content: What does the word “his” refer to in Paragraph 2 (“His Olympic success…”)?
options: A. Henrik Harlaut’s
B. Birk Ruud’s
C. Colby Stevenson’s
D. the United States

questions.content: Which detail from Paragraph 3 best illustrates why Stevenson’s Olympic success was considered unexpected?
options: A. He had competed internationally for many years
B. He returned to skiing sooner than doctors predicted
C. He trained exclusively for big air after the accident
D. He overcame injuries that threatened his career

questions.content: Which of the following is OPPOSITE in meaning to the word “resilience” as used in Paragraph 4?
options: A. fragility
B. endurance
C. persistence
D. stability
